procedure.method: Fresh independent review in this session, with no spawn, fork, resume or peer review. Read the pinned packet, case, rules, rubric, addendum and all five pinned native-evidence manifests; did not follow their unlisted embedded paths. The packet declares no source assets or protected layouts, so the corresponding receipts are explicitly empty. Opened and visually inspected each exact poster with tools.view_image(detail='original'), forwarding the returned image at original detail, in member order M1, M2, M3, M4, M5 and, within each, native then usage720 then thumbnail320. All fifteen opens completed before the first actual copy-reading/transcription stage, any judgment or score. Native views were 1672×941 for M1/M2 and 1024×1536 for M3/M4/M5; usage views were 720×405 and 720×1080 respectively; thumbnails were 320×180 and 213×320. Hash/byte and PNG-header checks corroborated the bindings and sizes but are not substituted for the actual visual opens. First readings used the already displayed native/usage pixels after the full opening sequence; no ambiguity-triggered revisit was needed. No source identity, omitted copy, maker intent, event or runtime session ID was inferred. The seven ratings and whole-set comparison below are my own pixel-based judgments.

evidence.location: right two-thirds and foreground
evidence.observation: Glass reflects people, vehicles and a lit tree above a large stone sill; textured pavement and long shadows fill the foreground. These nonglyph elements carry the discovery of light and human traces along an ordinary street.

evidence.location: window reflection, sill and pavement
evidence.observation: The street's doubled reflection and diagonal light/shadow route are readable and occupy most of the poster, making attentive walking specific rather than relying on the title alone.

content_form.location: glass at right and paving foreground
content_form.observation: The reflected walkers and cars, direct pavement and long light bands reward looking at an ordinary route from more than one angle; the nonglyph scene closely supports finding new stories in familiar surroundings.

hierarchy.location: upper-left copy block to right-hand sill
hierarchy.observation: The large two-line title leads to the body, then the curb carries the eye toward the reflected street. Image contrast is strongest mainly outside the body block.
The title remains the first readable typographic element; the scene still holds the other half of attention.

typography.observation: The Korean title has coherent serif stroke modulation and open counters; body glyphs, commas, periods and word gaps are intact.
The full body is easy to continue reading at this width, with consistent leading and no visible shadow crossing that destroys a word.

space.location: left text inset and diagonal sill
space.observation: The repeated left inset and compact copy block are balanced by the long, receding stone sill. The large pavement foreground is active with directed shadows rather than an unexplained blank.

image_material.location: stone sill, metal frame and glass
image_material.observation: Pebbled stone, smooth metal and transparent reflections have distinct surface responses to the same warm light; the scene remains coherent despite shallow focus in the distant street.

emotion_control.location: golden foreground and small reflected pedestrians
emotion_control.observation: Warm light and low pavement viewpoint create a welcoming, observant pause; the public street remains present without dominating the quiet surface study.

ai_slop.observation: Frames and paving recede consistently, and the reflection belongs to the glass. No arbitrary decorative marks or clearly contradictory foreground construction are visible; distant figures are softened by depth of field rather than resolved portraits.

residuals: The warm street photograph and conventional title/body setting are professionally coherent, but do not establish exceptional typographic or editorial invention.
Distant reflected figures and storefront detail are optically soft; no exact identity or unreadable sign copy is inferred.
Native 1672×941 is accepted as 16:9 by nearest-integer single-edge rounding: ideal height at width 1672 is 940.5, a 0.5 px difference. It is not mathematically exact 16:9.

evidence.observation: The framed luminous window, plant and furniture shapes, curb and reflected pavement carry light and human traces at substantial scale; lettering is only one part of the composition.

evidence.location: warm vertical window and lower reflected light
evidence.observation: The light travels from a recognizable street window into the uneven paving, sustaining the urban observation even when fine paint detail is reduced.

content_form.observation: Looking from a small sign of interior life to its broken reflection in an ordinary street surface embodies discovering a new story while passing a familiar corner.

hierarchy.observation: Cream type leads cleanly against the darkest area, while the window becomes the main image focus and its reflection pulls attention down the street.
The title is immediate and the bright window is a clear secondary anchor; neither dissolves into the brushwork.

typography.location: cream serif title and sans-serif body
typography.observation: The headline's modulated Korean strokes are coherent, and the body retains all glyphs, word spaces, commas and periods.
All four lines remain readable, with enough contrast and consistent leading despite the textured wall.

space.location: dark left wall and lower pavement
space.observation: The upper text area is proportioned to the window, and the lower pavement is occupied by reflected light and a receding curb. Dark space supports the copy while remaining part of the street.

image_material.location: window mullions, plant, curb and light patches
image_material.observation: Broad paint handling changes direction across upright wall/window forms and flatter wet stones. The warmer interior and cooler exterior remain structurally and materially coherent.

emotion_control.location: warm window, quiet dark wall and broken golden reflection
emotion_control.observation: The narrow inhabited glow against the cool dark street makes a precise sense of passing near someone else's life. The reflection carries that warmth toward the viewer without crowding the calm reading area.
The intimate nocturnal effect survives removal of brush detail: a concentrated warm source, dark surroundings and a descending trail of light remain exceptionally clear and controlled.

ai_slop.location: window frame, sill, wall corner and wet stones
ai_slop.observation: The major painted forms remain mutually consistent, and the interior silhouettes supply human presence without random objects multiplying across the street. Brush abstraction does not obscure the window or curb's role.

residuals: The plant and furniture are abbreviated painted silhouettes; no exact interior activity is inferred from them.
The image and emotional control are stronger than the conventional typography, which is resolved but not exceptional.
Native 1024×1536 is mathematically exact 2:3; the 213×320 thumbnail rounds the short edge.

Its abrasive high-contrast print identity and direct downward viewpoint distinguish it from M3's pale drawn doorway and the other three.

evidence.location: large drain at upper-right and cracked paving through lower field
evidence.observation: Recognizable elongated drain slots, paving seams, erosion and the diagonal light band form substantive nonglyph content across the canvas; the print speckle is subordinate to those objects.

evidence.location: right drain and crossing sunlit pavement
evidence.observation: The drain's dark intervals and the light exposing worn joints reveal an everyday piece of street infrastructure at meaningful scale, supporting attention to overlooked traces.

content_form.location: grate, eroded seams and light band
content_form.observation: The downward crop invites noticing the familiar ground underfoot. Worn stone and a drain create concrete urban traces, while a strong strip of light reframes those ordinary details.

hierarchy.observation: The short one-line title and four-line body form a compact entry, then the large black slots and diagonal light lead across the image.
The title remains a clear anchor even at its smaller apparent scale; the grate continues to register as the primary image shape.

typography.location: heavy serif title and sans-serif body
typography.observation: The Korean title has a cohesive heavy serif voice, with clear counters and word gaps; the body is structurally consistent and punctuation is intact.
All body lines remain comfortable to read and the background speckling does not materially cross or erase the glyphs.

space.location: lit upper-left pavement, grate crop and diagonal lower light
space.observation: The copy sits in a coherent illuminated patch, balanced by the large grate and by the diagonal across the lower field. The cropped grate implies continuation beyond the frame.

image_material.location: rough cream/teal pavement and near-black drain slots
image_material.observation: The granular print treatment and hard value separation describe an abrasive street surface; clear grate and joint shapes keep the texture attached to real objects rather than a decorative noise field.

emotion_control.location: dark rough paving and cream diagonal
emotion_control.observation: The sharp light and coarse surface create concentrated, gritty curiosity about what is normally overlooked. The cream copy area gives the dense ground enough relief for the invitation to remain accessible.

ai_slop.location: grate outline and connected paving seams
ai_slop.observation: The slotted grate is recognizable and the major seams join into an intelligible ground surface. Repeated speckle is extensive but follows the print treatment rather than introducing arbitrary ornaments or contradictory objects.

residuals: The granular treatment gives several materials a similar roughness, reducing local tonal nuance; the drain and paving remain identifiable.
The heavier title differentiates its voice, though it retains the set's familiar upper-left title/body organization.
Native 1024×1536 is mathematically exact 2:3; thumbnail 213×320 rounds the short edge.

recording_adapter.limit: Metadata bindings and attestations do not prove semantic viewing or source fidelity

evidence.location: street panorama and mirrored glass
evidence.observation: The warm photographic public street, deep reflections and long pavement shadows give M1 an observational daylight identity. Compared with M3's tight drawn threshold, it uses believable street depth and actual-looking reflected activity rather than isolated wear.

evidence.location: yellow/navy perspective and red prints
evidence.observation: M2's saturated planar contrast, monumental gothic line and distressed sole route form the most outward and graphic identity. Its simplified light/shadow geometry and walking marks differ in construction, emotional energy and type voice from all four surface scenes.

evidence.location: pale cracked wall, door handle and step
evidence.observation: M3's fine contour drawing, light washes, blue/cream relationship and serif body create quiet close observation of use and age. It shares a legible upper-left reading order with M1/M4, but its object intimacy, surface drawing and daylight restraint are distinct from their photographic public depth and painted night warmth.

evidence.location: dark wall, lit window and golden pavement
evidence.observation: M4's heavy brush marks, cool-dark/amber relationship and luminous occupied window give an intimate nocturnal identity. The emotional center is interior life reflecting outward, unlike M3's weathered threshold or M5's abrasive infrastructure; its similar two-line title layout does not erase that difference.

evidence.location: overhead drain, rough print and diagonal cream band
evidence.observation: M5 has hard printed value separation, coarse teal/cream/black surface, a downward crop and heavier one-line serif anchor. Compared with M3, the object, viewing angle, tonal force, glyph weight and emotional abrasion change together; this is more than adding a filter to the same doorway composition.

residuals: All five use a left-aligned title followed immediately by a four-line body; M1/M3/M4 also have closely related serif headline voices. This shared functional order is allowed, but limits the set's typographic breadth.

M1/M3/M4/M5 all study street surfaces or building edges. Their differing scene relationships, image construction, light/contrast and emotional effects achieve five recognizable identities, while the common observational family keeps diversity at 4 rather than exceptional 5.
The five members and this single editorial review are fully assessed. No claim is made about the two other critics, their scores, the all-three gate or unseen requests.
